item.title: Ukraine refuses EU requests to inspect damaged Druzhba pipeline
item.description: The European Union is stepping up pressure on Ukraine to permit independent inspection of the Druzhba oil pipeline, which has been out of service since a Russian strike on January 27 disrupted the flow of crude to Hungary and Slovakia. Kyiv has repeatedly refused access requests on security grounds, fueling a dispute that has stalled a €90 billion EU aid package for Ukraine.

item.title: Macron deploys aircraft carrier to Mediterranean amid Middle East crisis
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron announced on Tuesday the deployment of France's nuclear-powered aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle to the Mediterranean, marking a major European military escalation as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran enters its fourth day. In a televised address from the Élysée Palace, Macron said the carrier, along with its Rafale fighter jets, air defense systems, airborne radar, and escorting frigates, had been ordered to leave its exercises in the North Atlantic and Baltic Sea and sail south immediately.

"Confronted with this volatile environment and the unpredictability of the days ahead, I have commanded the aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle, along with its air resources and frigate escort, to embark for the Mediterranean," Macron said.

item.title: Iranian drone strikes US Consulate in Dubai as war widens across Gulf
item.description:
A drone struck the parking area of the US Consulate in Dubai late Tuesday, igniting a fire that was quickly extinguished by emergency teams, as Iran's retaliatory campaign against American interests across the Gulf expanded into its fourth day following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

No casualties were reported, according to both a US official and Dubai's government media office. Videos geolocated to the consulate showed dark smoke rising from near the compound. The attack came as Iran continued to unleash projectiles on the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states in retaliation for the US-Israeli military operation that began February 28.

item.title: Macron orders evacuations, deploys forces as Iran conflict strands hundreds of thousands
item.description: Governments across Europe scrambled on Tuesday to repatriate hundreds of thousands of their citizens stranded in the Middle East, as widespread airspace closures triggered by the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran left travelers and residents unable to return home.

item.title: Israel says it destroyed secret Iranian nuclear site near Tehran
item.description:
The Israeli military announced on Tuesday that its air force destroyed a secret Iranian nuclear weapons development facility on the outskirts of Tehran, marking the first public acknowledgment that Iran had begun rebuilding weapons capabilities dismantled during last year's 12-day war.

IDF Chief Spokesman Brig. Gen. Effie Defrin identified the partially underground facility as "Min Zadai," located on the northeast outskirts of the Iranian capital. According to the IDF, a group of nuclear scientists had been "working secretly to develop capabilities required for nuclear weapons" at the compound. Israeli intelligence tracked the scientists as they attempted to travel to the site clandestinely, ultimately revealing the nature of the work being conducted there.

item.title: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of drone attacks in its civil war
item.description:
Sudan's army-backed government has formally accused Ethiopia of allowing drones to be launched from its territory to strike targets inside Sudan, marking the first time Khartoum has directly implicated its neighbor in the nearly three-year-old civil war.

In a statement issued Monday, March 2, the Sudanese Foreign Ministry said the government had been "monitoring, throughout February and into early March, the ongoing unauthorized entry of unmanned aircraft (drones) from inside Ethiopian territory into Sudanese airspace, targeting locations within Sudan". The ministry described the incursions as "a flagrant violation of Sudan's sovereignty and a clear act of aggression against the Sudanese state".

The statement did not specify who carried out the attacks, how many occurred, or which locations were hit. However, according to Reuters, the southeastern Blue Nile state, which borders Ethiopia, has seen small skirmishes and drone attacks in recent weeks. Parts of Blue Nile are controlled by the SPLM-N rebel group, which aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces last year.

item.title: Afreximbank raises Caribbean financing cap to $5B
item.description: The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) has increased its financing ceiling for the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) from $3 billion to $5 billion, marking the latest expansion of economic ties between Africa and the Caribbean diaspora.

item.title: Top U.S. general details timeline of Iran strikes
item.description: The United States and Israel launched a massive coordinated military assault against Iran on February 28, 2026, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior officials in an operation that has plunged the Middle East into its most serious conflict in decades. Now entering its fourth day, the war has drawn in Gulf Arab states through Iranian retaliatory strikes and sparked fierce international debate over its legality and endgame.

item.title: Syria deploys thousands of troops to Lebanon border
item.description: Syria has reinforced its border with Lebanon by deploying thousands of soldiers, rocket units, and armored vehicles, according to a Reuters report citing eight Syrian and Lebanese sources. The buildup began in February but accelerated in recent days as hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah intensified across the region.

item.title: Iran threatens to attack any ship in Strait of Hormuz as Asia scrambles for energy
item.description:
Asian governments and energy companies are racing to secure alternative oil and gas supplies as the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz following U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran threatens to choke off the region's most critical energy artery. With Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps officials declaring the strait "closed" and warning that any vessel attempting to pass would be attacked, the world's most oil-dependent economies face their most serious supply disruption in decades.

The strait, a narrow passage between Iran and Oman, typically carries roughly 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas. An estimated 84% of crude oil and 83% of LNG transiting the waterway is destined for Asian markets, with China, India, Japan, and South Korea accounting for an estimated 69% of oil and 59% of LNG flows.

item.title: Iran's Assembly of Experts elects Mojtaba Khamenei as next supreme leader
item.description:
Iran's Assembly of Experts has elected Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as the next leader of the Islamic Republic under pressure from the Revolutionary Guards, according to Iran International, citing informed sources. The reported selection, which has not been officially confirmed by Iranian state media, came even as Israeli airstrikes struck the very building where the clerical body had gathered to count votes in the holy city of Qom.

The unconfirmed appointment would mark a dramatic and controversial hereditary transfer of power in a republic whose theocratic system has never before passed the supreme leadership from father to son.

item.title: Survey finds one in three European women face violence
item.description:
Roughly one in three women in the European Union have experienced physical or sexual violence in their lifetime, yet the vast majority of cases are never reported to authorities, according to a sweeping new survey released on March 3 by the EU Agency for Fundamental Rights and the European Institute for Gender Equality.

The report, titled "EU Gender-based Violence Survey: Evidence for Policy and Practice," draws on interviews with more than 114,000 women aged 18 to 74 conducted between September 2020 and March 2024 across all 27 member states. It found that 30.7% of women reported having experienced physical violence, threats, or sexual violence by any perpetrator — a figure that represents a slight decline from the 33% recorded in the inaugural survey conducted in 2012.

item.title: Merz meets Trump as Germany's military buildup reshapes Europe
item.description: As German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met with President Donald Trump at the White House on March 3, the visit underscored a striking transformation: Germany, long defined by post-war pacifism, is racing to build Europe's most powerful conventional military force. The ambition has drawn cautious applause from allies — but also quiet anxiety in capitals from Paris to Warsaw about what a heavily armed Germany means for the balance of power on the continent.

item.title: Turkey engaging all sides to end Iran war, foreign minister says
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Tuesday condemned the ongoing US-Israeli military offensive against Iran as a "clear violation" of international law and vowed to intensify diplomatic efforts to secure a ceasefire, as the conflict that began on February 28 showed no signs of abating.

item.title: Iran warns advanced weapons not yet deployed in conflict
item.description: Iran's Defense Ministry declared on Tuesday that the country has withheld its most advanced weapons systems as the US-Israeli military campaign enters its fourth day, directly countering President Donald Trump's assertions that Tehran's military capabilities have been neutralized.

item.title: Ship hit near UAE's Fujairah as Gulf attacks escalate
item.description: A commercial vessel was hit by an unknown projectile approximately 7 nautical miles east of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported on March 4. The ship's master reported that the projectile caused damage to the vessel's steel plating, though all crew members were safe with no fire or water ingress detected onboard, according to UKMTO.

item.title: Carney says US-Israel strikes on Iran appear to violate international law
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called on Wednesday for the "rapid de-escalation" of the conflict triggered by joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, saying the war represented "another example of the failure of the international order". Speaking at a press conference in Sydney, Australia, during an official visit, Carney offered his sharpest critique yet of how the military operation has been conducted, even as he reaffirmed Canada's support for neutralizing Iran's nuclear threat.

item.title: Google exposes iPhone exploit kit that spread from spies to criminals
item.description: A powerful iPhone hacking toolkit that appears to have originated in government surveillance operations has spread to foreign espionage groups and financially motivated cybercriminals, according to research published Tuesday by Google's Threat Intelligence Group and mobile security firm iVerify.

item.title: UN warns El Niño could return later this year
item.description:
The World Meteorological Organization warned on Tuesday that El Niño could develop later this year as the current La Niña weakens, a shift that climate scientists say could push global temperatures toward new records in 2027.

The WMO's latest update, issued March 3, forecasts a 60% chance of neutral conditions — neither El Niño nor La Niña — during March through May, rising to 70% during April through June. But the probability of El Niño increases steadily thereafter, reaching roughly 40% by May through July.

item.title: US and Ecuador launch joint military strikes on drug cartels
item.description:
Ecuadorian and U.S. military forces launched joint operations against designated terrorist organizations inside Ecuador on March 3, marking a new front in the South American nation's escalating war against drug cartels. The U.S. Southern Command announced the operations, calling them "a powerful example of the commitment of partners in Latin America and the Caribbean to combat the scourge of" narco-terrorism.

The launch follows a weekend of high-level meetings in Quito, where SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan met with President Daniel Noboa and senior defense officials on March 1-2 to finalize plans for security cooperation. Noboa announced the initiative on X, writing: "In March, we will carry out joint operations alongside our regional allies, including the United States".
